text: {"status":"contradicted","evidence_ids":["ev-ce41690aa36014fdb717d1b4"],"request_dft":false,"proposed_test_ids":[],"rationale":"The claim is that the archived ideal olivine LiFePO4 calculation represents AFM Fe ordering, with a net cell moment of at most 0.5 muB. The converged DFT record (ionic accuracy reached, max force 0.0096 eV/A, which is below the 0.01 threshold) reports total_magnetization_abs = 16.0 muB for the Li4Fe4P4O16 cell. That value is exactly 4 Fe x 4 muB, the fully ferromagnetic high-spin Fe2+ moment. It is far above the 0.5 muB threshold. The input settings also initialize all Fe moments parallel at 5.0 muB, which is an FM start. A calculation started FM and relaxed to a 16 muB net moment is an FM solution, so the archived calculation does not represent AFM ordering. The decision quantity, structure and unit all match the criterion, and the record is a converged DFT relaxation, so it is admissible and there is no conflicting record. The verdict therefore rests on the evidence and needs no further test. An AFM versus FM comparison could show which ordering is lower in energy, but that is a different question from what this archived calculation represents. I do not request DFT, since the claim about this specific archived calculation is already decided. No peers have spoken, so I have no peer claims to support or dispute. The remaining assumption is that the reported total_magnetization_abs is the net cell moment and not a sum of absolute site moments. A sum of absolute site moments could be large even for AFM. However, 16.0 is an integer matching the FM expectation, and the FM initialization supports that reading. A falsification test would be to rerun with an AFM initialization (+/-) and check whether the net moment drops to about 0."}
